name: 立ち飲み餃子 大笑 (Tachinomi Gyoza Daisho)

claims.text: A gyoza-focused kitchen working constantly with wheat-flour wrappers; flour and wheat-based sauces are pervasive, so cross-contamination is effectively unavoidable.
No specific information published; as a Chinese-style izakaya, standard wheat-containing Japanese/Chinese soy sauce should be assumed.
Meat-centric menu (meat-filled gyoza, stamina gyoza, Chinese oden); no vegan options documented and shared cooking surfaces make plant-only dining impractical.

name: 大衆割烹 大関 (Taishu Kappo Ozeki)

claims.text: Oden, simmered dishes, and sauce-glazed eel are built on wheat-based soy sauce and fish dashi; there is no separate gluten-free preparation.
Eel is offered sauce-glazed (kabayaki style) and dishes use standard soy-based seasonings, which contain wheat.
The oden broth and most dishes are made with fish/seafood dashi, and the kitchen centers on eel, crab, and seafood; vegan separation is not possible.

name: 大衆割烹 魚吟 (Taishu Kappo Uogin)

claims.text: Soy-sauce- and dashi-based seafood cooking throughout; sashimi and grilled dishes are served with soy sauce, and oden is simmered in fish sauce — high gluten exposure with no documented gluten-free handling.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used for sashimi and grilled dishes; no gluten-free tamari mentioned.
Menu is built on fish, seafood, and fish-based dashi/ishiru stock; no vegan or vegetarian dishes documented.

name: 大衆酒場魚八 (Taishu Sakaba Uohachi)

claims.text: Fried Kaga lotus root and megisu fritters share the kitchen; no dedicated gluten-free preparation is documented.
Sashimi and seared fish are served with soy sauce, which in Japan is typically wheat-based; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The kitchen is seafood-centric (sashimi, grilled fish, dashi-based dishes), so vegan cross-contact risk is high and no plant-only preparation is documented.

name: 手打ち蕎麦 ほやさけ (Teuchi Soba Hoyasake)

claims.text: No gluten-free measures documented; soba and udon plus wheat-based tsuyu and tempura share the same kitchen.
Broths and dipping sauces are dashi/soy-based and not specified as wheat-free; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Noodle broths typically use bonito (fish) dashi; no vegan or plant-based broth is documented.

name: 手打蕎麦 こより (Teuchi Soba Koyori)

claims.text: Soba noodles are buckwheat-based but the kitchen also fries tempura and uses wheat-containing soy sauce in the broth; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
The dipping broth is finished with local round-soybean soy sauce, which contains wheat.
The broth is built on bonito and mackerel dashi, and duck dishes are a specialty, so animal products are central to the menu.
Several signature sweets are naturally starch-based rather than wheat-based: honkuzukiri is made from Yoshino arrowroot (kudzu) and honwarabimochi from bracken starch, with kinako and kuromitsu.
Coffee is paired with seasonal Japanese sweets like yokan and zenzai, several of which are traditionally plant-based, though the specific items are chosen by the house and not selectable.
